submission.justification: T1 has the best resolution (6 um) but fails the hard efficiency requirement, at 82% after 2e16 neq/cm^2. Of the two that pass, T3 has better resolution than T2 (9 um vs 14 um) and has 98.5% efficiency, above the 97% limit. I chose 150 um because that is the only thickness with resolution data. This is not an optimised value. I had no simulation tool, so I did not scan thickness. The documents don't give the thickness used for the irradiation efficiency measurement. The 98.5% margin at 150 um is therefore unverified and should be checked.

requirements.evidence: T3 has 9 um at 150 um, unirradiated. This is the best of the candidates that pass the efficiency requirement. T1 is better (6 um) but is excluded.
T3 measured 98.5% in the 2026 test beam. The thickness of the tested sensors is not stated, so this is unverified at exactly 150 um.

requirements.requirement: Technology is one of the three candidates
